PullRequest.Title: Add GitHub prompt variation to the V3 onboarding tour
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- add `prompt` and `githubPrompt` variations to the V3 new-session onboarding tour
- select recent actionable GitHub PRs or issues with independent bounded lookups and prompt fallback
- wait for Agent Host session types and publish draft Git/GitHub metadata before onboarding runs
- resolve GitHub repository identity from session metadata, GitHub workspace URIs, or `.git/config`
- add prompt-strategy telemetry and filterable diagnostics

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- focused onboarding, GitHub fetcher, repository resolver, and Agent Host unit tests

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new resolver accepts no cancellation token and awaits each parent stat without checking cancellation. The caller explicitly cancels on its six-second deadline, and the run-step presentation also cancels on dismissal. Remote Agent Host stat maps directly to an uncached resourceResolve request, establishing the continued I/O independently of its measured duration.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Remote resourceResolve requests and filesystem stat/read operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For a selected folder without a nearby .git entry, work is one serial stat per visited parent, bounded by the directory depth and 50 iterations. All remaining iterations can still execute after cancellation; there is no positive/negative cache or coalescing in this resolver.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unnecessary remote and filesystem I/O continues after dismissal or fallback, consuming the connection and remote host resources needed by ongoing work.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The V3 tour inserted its static prompt without traversing parent directories or issuing repository-discovery filesystem requests.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: GitHub prompt discovery now traverses parent directories even after its owning tour has been cancelled or its total lookup timeout has selected the fallback prompt.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added loop at lines 54–56 schedules sequential statIfExists calls for up to 50 parents. The added caller at newSessionViewV3Prompt.ts:427 does not pass its token; cancellation at :181 therefore cannot stop subsequent iterations.
Findings.Title: Cancel the parent-directory scan with the onboarding lookup
Findings.Impact: Dismiss the tour while it is discovering a nested remote workspace, or let discovery exceed the six-second timeout on a slow connection. The prompt flow has already stopped or fallen back, but the scan continues sending requests through the remaining ancestors.
Findings.Evidence: newSessionViewV3Prompt.ts:170–185 races discovery against a timeout and cancels operationCts; :395 checks cancellation only before entering repository resolution, then :427 awaits the tokenless resolver. gitHubRepositoryResolver.ts:52–76 checks only iteration count and filesystem root. FileService.stat delegates to provider.stat (fileService.ts:313–318); AHPFileSystemProvider.stat calls _resolve (agentHostFileSystemProvider.ts:387–404), which sends connection.resourceResolve (:615–616), and RemoteAgentHostProtocolClient.resourceResolve sends a protocol request (:1161–1162). RunOnboardingStepPresentation.runStep races the callback against cancellation, so dismissal does not wait for this scan.
Findings.Recommendation: Thread the lookup token through git-config discovery, check it before each stat/read and after awaited operations, and recheck it before entering the Git-extension fallback. Individual stats need not gain a cancellation API; stop scheduling additional operations once the current one settles.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents window startup, provider readiness, and V2/V3 tour eligibility
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The BlockRestore contribution binds a context key and synchronously reads advertised provider session types. Tours wait for a usable Agent Host type, existing restore completion, entitlement, and workspace-picker readiness; it does not await a new host connection.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered providers and advertised types, scanned on session-type change events; one readiness contribution per window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous event callback and one scan per session-type event; no asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reads providers' current in-memory sessionTypes. No added disk/network cache, initialization request, or negative lookup retry; context-key updates reflect provider events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: contribution, SessionsManagementService constructor, and getAllProviderSessionTypes were inspected; the changed callback collects existing state rather than requesting it.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider/type counts and event frequency vary; no measured startup cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: readiness adds a bounded in-memory scan and owned listener, not a new connection or subprocess launch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Default prompt variation and prompt animation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The run step now resolves a variation treatment, then two template/placeholder treatments in parallel, before the existing 2.5-second animation. Treatment reads can wait for the assignment service's existing initial fetch on a cold missing key. Animation remains cancellable and respects user edits.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read treatment values from TAS cache or await its shared initial fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three new logical treatment reads per normal prompt run; they share the service's single initial fetch, not one HTTP call per treatment. The template and placeholder reads are parallel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prompt was static and required no run-step treatment reads. Existing experiment eligibility already read behavior and assignment-context treatments using the same service/fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These reads precede insertion; warm reads are in-memory, while cold missing keys can await existing initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit a fixed-shape categorical strategy telemetry record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small strategy event per completed run; treatment reads also emit their existing fixed-shape telemetry events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No strategy event; existing onboarding and assignment telemetry remained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Strategy telemetry occurs after animation, not before prompt insertion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One eligible tour run per shared seen key, three treatment keys, and prompt text length. Animation performs at most one write per scheduled frame over the unchanged duration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Variation read is awaited first; two template reads then run concurrently. Animation has one pending frame and disposes it on cancellation or user edits.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Assignment service uses warm cached values, an existing shared initial fetch for cold reads, and configuration overrides. The pair falls back atomically to defaults. No new per-key cache or retained histories.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call placement and shared fetch behavior; no evidence of independent network fetches per treatment or changed animation scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold assignment-fetch delay and treatment text lengths are unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: required configuration reads share existing assignment initialization, and passing changed prompt copy into the existing animator does not establish amplified rendering work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Personalized GitHub prompt from published metadata or a cloud GitHub URI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve the variation and repository identity, fetch issue and PR summaries independently, select failing CI first, then await review candidates if necessary, then use the issue result. Sub-lookups have 2.5-second summary/review and 1.5-second linkage deadlines under a six-second total deadline, before animation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Silently obtain existing GitHub authentication sessions, including the authentication-provider extension-host boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One silent authentication lookup per attempted GraphQL request: normally two summary lookups, up to one linkage lookup and five review lookups; no session-creation request on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The static prompt did not obtain GitHub authentication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authentication precedes each HTTP request. Missing authentication terminates each bounded summary lookup without issuing GraphQL HTTP requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch two recent-work summaries, one batched issue-linkage query if needed, and separate PR review-thread queries if needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most eight GraphQL requests per repository attempt: two summaries, zero or one linkage request covering up to five issues together, and zero to five review requests. CI success exits without review queries and cancels remaining issue work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No recent-user-work GitHub requests on the V3 prompt path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required results are awaited before candidate insertion, with independent deadlines and a total deadline.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize GraphQL variables and parse/map bounded query responses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most five issues, five PR summaries, and 100 threads with one comment each per reviewed PR; linkage selections are batched for the five issue numbers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No GitHub query serialization for the static prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Response parsing completes within the lookup path before candidate selection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected repository; search queries cap each summary at five items, review queries cap threads at 100, and issue linkage is grouped into one request. Context changes can cause another attempt within the total deadline.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Two summary requests begin together. Up to five review lookups run in Promise.all while the issue pipeline may still have one request in flight, giving at most six concurrent GraphQL operations per attempt. There is no added global limiter, but query cardinality provides this bound. Each attempt cancels outstanding issue work in finally.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Recent-work methods have no result or negative cache, and HTTP cache is bypassed. The tour's once-per-user/window gating bounds normal invocation. Repository metadata/cloud URI resolution is entirely in-memory. Existing auth-provider state is reused without prompting.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: fetcher queries, API implementation, runner ordering, and tests demonstrate effective grouping, caps, cancellation, and fallback.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GitHub latency and the distribution of users with five authored PRs are unknown; query and concurrency bounds are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No fan-out finding: requests are intentionally bounded and issue linkage is batched; there is no unbounded per-history-item boundary or retained cache growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: GitHub repository discovery from local or remote .git/config and Git-extension fallback
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When metadata and cloud URIs do not resolve identity, the new resolver walks parents sequentially, then reads config or worktree indirection files. Agent Host drafts subsequently wait for published metadata; non-Agent-Host drafts can call GitService.openRepository. This discovery precedes GitHub requests and animation under the total deadline.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat each parent's .git entry and read config, or .git/commondir/config worktree indirection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: D explicit sequential stats, with D bounded by the distance to .git or filesystem root and 50. An ordinary repository needs one config read; a worktree can need three reads. FileService read validation can add metadata operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The static prompt performed no repository-discovery filesystem operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The serial chain is awaited before repository selection; the outer six-second race bounds foreground waiting but not these underlying operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve metadata and read files over the remote Agent Host connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One uncached resourceResolve per explicit remote stat, plus file-read/validation requests. Calls remain sequential across visited ancestors; there is no repository grouping that reduces D.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No discovery requests over the remote connection from the prompt step.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each round trip delays the next ancestor probe. Published metadata is only checked again after config discovery completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open a repository through the Git extension and obtain its repository state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one Git-extension open per non-Agent-Host repository-resolution attempt after the config route fails. Main-thread opens are globally sequenced; Agent Host drafts take the metadata-wait branch instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The static prompt did not open repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited on this discovery path; GitService may wait for its existing delegate barrier, and the tour deadline can expire first.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: If not already open, initialize the Git repository via existing root/.git discovery and asynchronous initial status.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical repository open per fallback attempt. Existing exact-repository checks avoid repeated initialization; cold initialization may run existing Git probes rather than one subprocess per workspace file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These Git operations existed for other workflows but were not requested by the V3 prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Root/open work is awaited; initial status is scheduled by the existing limiter and is not directly awaited by Model.openRepository.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Directory depth to repository/root, ordinary versus worktree checkout, remote round-trip time, and whether the Git extension already has that repository open.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Parent traversal and worktree reads are serial. Git extension opens use the existing main-thread sequencer and extension model sequencing; existing cold initial status uses its limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No positive/negative cache in git-config discovery. FileService.stat delegates to providers; remote resourceResolve is not cached. Git-extension exact-repository checks reuse existing repository initialization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for new boundary placement, sequential cardinality, and provider delegation; no subprocess count or latency benchmark is asserted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Directory depth and local/remote latency vary. Normal nearby .git discovery is small; slow deep paths can exceed the total foreground deadline.
Scenarios.Verdict: Discovery itself is bounded and required for the new feature; the actionable regression is its failure to stop scheduling operations after cancellation, reported separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dismissal, timeout, or workspace replacement during personalized lookup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Run-step dismissal races cancellation so the UI can proceed immediately. The total GitHub timeout selects the default prompt at six seconds. Repository-context changes cause a bounded retry after the current awaited lookup and cancel that attempt's outstanding GitHub work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Continue remote ancestor metadata requests after the owning lookup has been cancelled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for each remaining parent after the in-flight stat settles, up to the remaining D within the 50-iteration cap; reads can also continue if a .git entry is found. No caching or coalescing eliminates them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cancellation stopped the existing prompt animation; no directory-discovery request chain existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: After dismissal/fallback this is off the original critical path, but continues consuming remote connection and filesystem resources. A slow lookup can outlive the foreground deadline.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Remaining directory depth when cancellation occurs, multiplied by remote round-trip latency. A typical nested remote workspace is sufficient; reaching the maximum cap is not required.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The offending directory requests remain serial but continue being newly scheduled after cancellation. GitHub requests are independently bounded and cancelled on timeout/attempt completion; workspace retries are sequential and share the total time budget.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tokenless directory discovery has no cached positive or negative results. In contrast, HTTP requests receive cancellation tokens and the browser implementation checks already-cancelled tokens and aborts active fetches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the caller cancels explicitly, the presentation stops waiting, and the new resolver accepts no token or cancellation checks while the provider sends uncached requests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: How often users dismiss during discovery or use slow deep remote paths is unknown; the number of remaining requests and their duration are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity introduced cleanup-lifecycle I/O regression with a bounded fix: stop issuing additional stats/reads when cancellation is observed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Publishing Git/GitHub metadata to an eager Agent Host draft and reacting to later updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An incoming existing SessionState now applies metadata to the draft workspace synchronously, allowing onboarding to consume it before the first message. No new backend git-state refresh is requested by the changed callback.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of incoming draft state updates, folder count copied into the workspace, and PR/issue references parsed from existing metadata. Workspace publication happens only when structural comparison detects a change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-state synchronous application. Existing backend git-state refreshes and their throttling are unchanged; the changed path consumes already-published state rather than adding subprocess/IPC calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Draft workspace retains its latest value, not a history. sessionWorkspaceEqual suppresses identical publications. Existing GitHub derived identities use structural equality and model references; merely adding repository identity without a PR does not start PR/CI/review polling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: NewSession.applySessionMeta, its state callback, workspace equality, composer consumers, and GitHub model/polling identity gates were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Draft update frequency and metadata sizes vary; no measured CPU/GC cost. Typical folder and reference counts are small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent performance regression: bounded metadata copies and structural notification suppression do not demonstrate amplified heavyweight work or unbounded retention.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete 27-file inventory and all diff pages in a distinct performance pass. Traced onboarding eligibility, assignment reads, bounded GitHub queries, local/remote repository discovery, cancellation, animation, and draft metadata publication. Submitted one introduced cleanup-lifecycle I/O regression. No concrete performance-regression fix with sufficient provenance was identified. Analysis is static; durations and prevalence were not measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
